points_of_disagreement: Whether the root cause of unrest is government unpreparedness/intelligence failure vs. socioeconomic grievance vs. immigration policy
Whether curfews are an appropriate emergency response or an authoritarian overreach that violates civil liberties
Whether the unrest represents legitimate mass protest or criminal rioting that justifies law-and-order measures
Whether the crisis is primarily a policy failure or a political opportunity being exploited by competing electoral factions
Whether proposed restrictions on voting rights and social media access are justified security measures or authoritarian tools

disagreements_detail.statement: What caused the unrest: government intelligence failure and unpreparedness vs. genuine socioeconomic grievance (cost of living, education) vs. immigration and integration failure
Whether curfews are an appropriate emergency response vs. an authoritarian overreach violating civil liberties
Whether the unrest is a legitimate mass movement with valid demands vs. criminal rioting requiring law-and-order measures
Whether the crisis is fundamentally a policy/governance failure vs. a political opportunity being weaponized by competing factions
Whether proposed restrictions on voting rights and social media access are justified security measures vs. authoritarian tools

shared_foundation.summary: All framings agree that civil unrest occurred in France, authorities proposed curfews, and the interior minister acknowledged some level of government unpreparedness. The disagreements are entirely interpretive: whether the unrest stems from economic hardship, immigration, or intelligence failure; whether curfews are justified or authoritarian; and whether the crisis is a genuine policy emergency or a political accelerant being exploited by competing electoral actors.

framings.name: Government Failure & Intelligence Breakdown
framings.short_label: Who let this spiral out of control?
framings.question: Did the French government and security services fail to anticipate and contain the unrest before curfews became necessary?
framings.key_claim: The Macron government's failure to read the severity of the protests — admitted by the interior minister himself — made curfews an emergency patch for a preventable crisis.
framings.traceable_claim: The French government failed to anticipate the severity of the October 2026 unrest, forcing emergency curfews as a reactive measure after authorities lost control in several cities.
framings.description: This framing centers on institutional accountability, foregrounding the interior minister's admission that police 'lost control' and that intelligence services underestimated the threat.
framings.emphasizes: Government unpreparedness, the interior minister's near-resignation, Macron's political exposure, and the reactive nature of the curfews
framings.downplays: The underlying socioeconomic grievances that drove protesters into the streets
sample_headlines: France moves to impose curfews as it reels from worst violence in years
Interior minister admits police 'lost control' during weekend riots

framings.name: Socioeconomic Grievance & Legitimate Protest
framings.question: Are the curfews suppressing a legitimate popular uprising rooted in economic inequality and failing public services?
framings.key_claim: The curfews criminalize a genuine mass movement of students and workers demanding relief from soaring costs and crumbling schools, treating symptoms rather than causes.
framings.traceable_claim: French curfews imposed after the October 2026 unrest are suppressing a legitimate popular uprising rooted in cost-of-living pressures and deteriorating public education.
framings.description: This framing treats the unrest as a rational response to structural economic failure, arguing that curfews address the violence while ignoring the underlying demands.
framings.emphasizes: Protesters' demands for better schools and cost-of-living relief, weak GDP growth, rising unemployment, and the government's inability to pass a budget
framings.downplays: Property destruction, looting, and the safety concerns of residents and businesses
sample_headlines: Why Is France Protesting? Riots, Curfews and the 2027 Race
Protesters are demanding better schools and relief from rising living costs

framings.name: Civil Liberties & State Overreach
framings.question: Do the curfews and protest bans constitute a disproportionate restriction on civil liberties and the right to assembly?
framings.key_claim: By banning demonstrations, imposing overnight curfews, and proposing to strip rioters of voting rights and social media access, the French state is deploying authoritarian tools against its own citizens.
framings.traceable_claim: The French government's October 2026 curfews and proposed measures — including stripping offenders of voting rights and restricting social media access — represent a disproportionate restriction on civil liberties.
framings.description: This framing scrutinizes the legal and democratic legitimacy of emergency restrictions, drawing on proposals by Justice Minister Darmanin that go well beyond the curfews themselves.
framings.emphasizes: Bans on public gatherings, proposals to remove voting rights, social media restrictions, and the historical precedent of France's 1955 emergency law being invoked
framings.downplays: The scale of violence and property destruction that prompted the measures
sample_headlines: Justice Minister proposes stripping rioters of voting rights and social media access

framings.name: Immigration & Law-and-Order
framings.short_label: Far right blames immigrants for riots
framings.question: Are the riots evidence that immigration and multiculturalism have produced an uncontrollable underclass that curfews alone cannot fix?
framings.key_claim: Right-wing politicians internationally are using the French unrest to argue that lax immigration policy — not economic inequality — is the root cause of the violence, and that curfews are too soft a response.
framings.traceable_claim: Right-wing politicians in the US, Spain, and Israel are using the October 2026 French riots to argue that immigration — not cost-of-living pressures — is the root cause of the unrest.
framings.description: This framing, amplified by far-right actors globally, reattributes the cause of the riots from economic grievance to immigration and cultural fragmentation, using France as a cautionary tale.
framings.emphasizes: Rioter demographics, looting footage, the perceived failure of French integration policy, and the inadequacy of curfews as a response
framings.downplays: The documented cost-of-living and education triggers, and the absence of any established link between immigration and the violence

framings.name: 2027 Presidential Race & Political Opportunism
framings.question: Are political actors — left, right, and center — exploiting the curfew crisis to position themselves ahead of the 2027 French presidential election?
framings.key_claim: The curfew crisis has become a political accelerant, with Le Pen polling ahead, Lecornu's government weakened, and every faction using the unrest to advance a pre-existing electoral narrative.
framings.traceable_claim: The October 2026 French curfew crisis is being exploited by all major political factions — including Le Pen's National Rally and the left — to advance their positioning ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
framings.description: This framing treats the curfews as a political event as much as a security one, mapping how the crisis reshuffles electoral dynamics and who benefits from Macron's weakened position.
framings.emphasizes: Le Pen's polling lead, Lecornu's vulnerability, the fractured parliament's inability to pass a budget, and the blame game between parties
framings.downplays: The immediate human and material costs of the unrest and the lived experience of affected communities

gap_analysis: Missing are framings centered on: (1) practical public safety concerns from residents and business owners in affected areas who may support targeted measures regardless of politics; (2) comparative international perspectives on curfew effectiveness and unintended consequences from other democracies; (3) the specific operational/logistical challenges authorities face in implementing such policies fairly; and (4) voices from within law enforcement expressing concerns about resource constraints, morale, or disagreement with the curfew approach itself rather than just political criticism.
